assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new classification of quantum matter: a clean, general model (Z2 invariant, protected helical edge states) with a universal, rigorously analysable structure, followed by a decisive experimental realisation. The idea has spread across solid-state, photonic and cold-atom systems and anchors the modern topological-materials field. This is the kind of simple mechanism with broad consequences that I value most.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical decisive step (quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 classification); Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental observation in HgTe/CdTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied credit supports a clean theory-plus-experiment trio. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu (3D) are not in the credited names, which leaves a real allocation question that I cannot resolve from this list.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed independently in several materials platforms for over fifteen years, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue, though it overlaps conceptually with the 2016 prize on topological phases.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz prize may be argued to dilute novelty.
Credit omits Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu, whose contributions were important; my knowledge of priority details is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, and the observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition made quantum simulation of many-body physics real. It connects statistical mechanics, condensed matter and atomic physics, and now supports studies of thermalisation, localisation and out-of-equilibrium dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition in a lattice (2002); Esslinger demonstrated Fermi gases in lattices and Mott states of fermions, and developed related quantum-simulation experiments. Zoller (with Jaksch et al.) proposed the lattice Hubbard realisation and is the key theoretical originator; leaving Zoller out is a choice, but a three-experimentalist trio is easier to defend than four names. Greiner's role is clearly decisive for the first observation, with Bloch as team leader.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, replicated across many groups, and now a mainstream field. The prize would be timely; some fraction of the credit already sits with the 2001 BEC and 2012 prizes, but the lattice simulation is a distinct step.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Peter Zoller as the theory originator, which would force a four-person configuration beyond the three-laureate limit.
Allocation between Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger is a judgement I cannot verify independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene produced flat bands and tunable correlated insulating and superconducting states in a single, simple material, launching moire quantum materials. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gives a clean, analysable mechanism for the flat bands at a magic angle, which is the sort of physical insight I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction (2011); Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity (2018). This theory-plus-experiment pairing supports a fair three-person prize. Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers (Cao, Fatemi) share the experimental credit, and the list's names cannot cover all of them.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly reproduced across many labs, yet the origin of superconductivity and the correlated phases is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet stable. The prize could be premature on the full phenomenon but is defensible for the flat-band prediction and its verification.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Sample-to-sample variability; whether the committee wants more time before recognition.
Other contributors (e.g. Santos and Peres, Lopes dos Santos, and the experimental junior authors) not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation is among the cleanest examples of non-equilibrium universality: a minimal stochastic model for interface growth whose scaling exponents and Tracy-Widom statistics are now exactly known in 1+1 dimensions, with deep links to random matrices, directed polymers and integrable systems. Takeuchi and Sano's liquid-crystal turbulence experiments confirmed the universal distributions quantitatively, and experiments in other systems (including quantum fluids) followed. Physically important and conceptually elegant, though its practical impact is narrower than the others on my list.
assessment.attribution: The equation is due to Kardar, Parisi and Zhang; Parisi is not among the credited names (and has already received the 2021 prize for other work), so the credited trio replaces him with Takeuchi, the experimental confirmer. This is an unusual configuration and Sano, Spohn, Corwin, Johansson, Sasamoto and Amir-Corwin-Quastel contributed to the exact solutions, so the allocation of credit is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Mature as theory and as experiment, with exact solutions and repeated confirmation, but experimental verification of the full universality class is recent (2010 onward), so recognition would be somewhat late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Parisi's exclusion from the credited names and the 2021 prize he already received make the attribution awkward.
Exact-solution contributors from mathematical physics are not represented in the credited names.
Broader impact beyond statistical physics is less direct.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming transition gave a unifying picture of rigidity in disordered matter, with critical scaling, isostaticity and an anomalous excess of low-frequency vibrational modes connecting granular matter, foams, emulsions and glasses. It fits my view that simple universal mechanisms can organise messy soft systems, and it has stimulated a large body of theory, simulation and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 proposal of a jamming phase diagram and subsequent work with O'Hern, Silbert and Wyart established the framework; the supplied two-name credit is clean, though important contributions from O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart, Torquato and others would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally and numerically well supported in idealised systems, but the connection to real glasses and the nature of the transition (is it a true critical point?) are still contested, and the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: The relation between jamming and the glass transition is unsettled.
Experimental tests in real granular systems are less sharp than for idealised models.
Credit omits O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart and Torquato.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases, from the Aharonov-Bohm effect to Berry's adiabatic phase, show that gauge structure and topology have observable consequences in quantum mechanics. This idea underlies much of modern condensed matter, including quantum Hall physics, topological insulators and polarisation theory, and it is conceptually foundational and rigorous.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) and Berry (1984) are decisive, but David Bohm is deceased and cannot be a laureate, while Pancharatnam, Simon and Wilczek-Zee are relevant to related parts of the story. The two-name credit is defensible for a combined geometric-phase prize, though the AB effect and Berry phase are distinct discoveries and the pairing feels somewhat constructed.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of experimental confirmation (Chambers, Tonomura, many optical and NMR experiments). Recognition would be late rather than premature, which is not a problem scientifically.
uncertainties: Whether the two effects should be recognised together as one prize.
Priority issues (Pancharatnam, Ehrenberg-Siday, Bohm's role) complicate attribution.
The committee may regard it as better suited to earlier decades.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory in two dimensions gave an exact description of critical phenomena, classifying universality classes through the Virasoro algebra and minimal models, and it underlies string theory and the physics of critical systems. It is the sharpest example of universality in statistical physics and has influenced several areas of physics and mathematics.
assessment.attribution: Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov (1984) wrote the foundational paper; the supplied trio is the natural configuration. Zamolodchikov died in 2025, to my recollection, which would be a problem for a living-laureate prize and which I flag as an unverified fact. Friedan, Qiu and Shenker, Cardy and others are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature; its predictions have been checked against exact lattice solutions and numerics rather than by a single decisive experiment, so empirical confirmation is indirect.
uncertainties: Possible death of one credited person, which I have not verified.
Weak direct experimental confirmation; recognition may be judged more mathematical than physical.
Contributions of Cardy, Friedan, Qiu and Shenker are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enable tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. The invention is original, clearly stated and has measurable and lasting impact in precision metrology.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and made the first demonstration; Ye's group drove the accuracy and stability to the current frontier. A two-person prize is fairly clean, though the 2005 prize (Hall and Hansch, frequency combs) and contributions from Lemonde, Derevianko and Kimble are adjacent.
assessment.maturity: Strong and independent confirmation from many national labs; the field is moving fast and a redefinition of the second is still pending, so the timing is reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 prize and with ion clocks (Wineland 2012) that may reduce novelty.
Impact beyond metrology is still prospective rather than established.
Competing optical-clock credit (ion clocks, Al+) is not covered by the supplied names.
